title: If, Else If, and Else
summary: Choose between branches with else and else if, nest decisions, and learn which values JavaScript treats as truthy or falsy.
intro: An `if` alone can only run code or skip it. With `else` and `else if` your program picks exactly one path out of several, and with truthy and falsy values you can test whether something is there at all.

steps.title: if and else

example.title: Odd or even
example.prompt: Print whether `n` is even or odd, and if it is odd, also say whether it is greater than 5.
example.explanation: `7 % 2` is `1`, so the condition `n % 2 === 0` is false and the `else` block runs, printing `7 is odd`. Inside that block a nested `if` asks a second question. `7 > 5` is true, so it prints the second line. With `n = 3` only the first line would print, and with `n = 8` the nested check would never run at all.

practice.title: Account balance
practice.prompt:
Report the state of a bank account with if, else, and a nested if.

1. Start with `const balance = -20;`
2. If `balance` is below `0`, print `Overdrawn`. Otherwise print `In credit`.
3. Inside the overdrawn branch only, also print `Fee applies` when `balance` is below `-10`.

Expected output:

```text
Overdrawn
Fee applies
```
hints: The outer condition asks whether `balance` is below `0`. Every other balance belongs in the `else` block.
Write the second `if (balance < -10)` inside the braces of the first branch, after printing `Overdrawn`.

steps.title: else if chains

example.title: Letter grade
example.prompt: Turn a numeric score into a letter grade with an else if chain.
example.explanation: `83 >= 90` is false, so JavaScript moves on. `83 >= 80` is true, so `grade` becomes `"B"` and the remaining checks are skipped, even though `83 >= 70` is also true. The thresholds go from highest to lowest, which is why each later check can stay simple: reaching it already means the score was below every earlier threshold.

practice.title: Shipping tier
practice.prompt:
Turn a parcel weight in kilograms into a shipping tier with an else if chain.

1. Start with `const weight = 7.5;` and `let tier;`
2. Set `tier` to `Small` when `weight` is at most `1`, `Medium` when at most `5`, `Large` when at most `20`, and `Freight` otherwise.
3. Print `Tier: ` followed by the tier.

Expected output:

```text
Tier: Large
```
hints: With `<=` the narrowest range is the lightest one, so check the smallest limit first.
Use `<=` in three conditions and put `tier = "Freight";` in the final `else`.

steps.title: Truthy and falsy

example.title: Boolean conversions
example.prompt: Print what `Boolean()` gives for several values, then greet a user whose name is empty.
example.output:
0 -> false
"" -> false
"0" -> true
null -> false
"hi" -> true
NaN -> false
Hello, guest
example.explanation: `0`, `""`, `null`, and `NaN` are on the falsy list, so `Boolean()` turns them into `false`. `"0"` is a non-empty string, so it is truthy even though it looks like zero. `username` is the empty string, which is falsy, so `if (username)` fails and the `else` branch prints `Hello, guest`.

practice.title: Double negation
practice.prompt:
Print what `!!` gives for several values, then report on an empty cart.

1. For `-1`, `undefined`, `"false"`, `0`, and `" "`, in that order, print one line each in the form `value -> result`, writing the value exactly as listed (strings keep their double quotes) and the result of `!!value`.
2. Declare `const itemsInCart = 0;`
3. Use `if (itemsInCart)` to print `Cart has ${itemsInCart} items`, and in the `else` branch print `Cart is empty`.

Expected output:

```text
-1 -> true
undefined -> false
"false" -> true
0 -> false
" " -> true
Cart is empty
```

tests.output:
-1 -> true
undefined -> false
"false" -> true
0 -> false
" " -> true
Cart is empty

hints: Copy the first line and change both the label and the value inside `${}`.
The label `"false"` is written with double quotes inside a template literal, which needs no escaping.
`0` is falsy, so `if (itemsInCart)` goes to the `else` branch.

recap:
- `if (...) { } else { }` runs exactly one of the two blocks.
- Nest an `if` inside a branch when a second question depends on the first.
- `else if` chains are checked top to bottom and the first true condition wins.
- Order conditions from most to least specific and end with `else` as the catch-all.
- Falsy values: `false`, `0`, `-0`, `""`, `null`, `undefined`, `NaN`. Everything else is truthy, even `"0"` and `" "`.
- `Boolean(value)` and `!!value` convert to a real boolean.
- `if (count)` treats a valid `0` as missing, so compare explicitly when `0` counts.
